content.text:
I found 4 warning logs, and all of them are the same kind of event: a checkout was rejected because product 2 was out of stock.

| # | Timestamp (Unix) | Event | User ID | Product ID | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1792108866.641 | checkout_rejected | 15 | 2 | out_of_stock |
| 2 | 1792108866.642 | checkout_rejected | 5 | 2 | out_of_stock |
| 3 | 1792108866.642 | checkout_rejected | 11 | 2 | out_of_stock |
| 4 | 1792108866.643 | checkout_rejected | 20 | 2 | out_of_stock |

All 4 happened within about 2 milliseconds, so several users tried to buy product 2 at almost the same moment after it had sold out. Rejecting them is the right result. But if this was a flash sale or a lot of people buying at once, you may want to make sure the item didn't get sold more times than you had in stock.

I can also look up the error logs or the successful checkouts for product 2 if you want to check that.
